phases.name: Ramp in
phases.note: Stop every set with 3 reps left. Week 1 is 2 sets, 3 sets from week 2.

phases.name: Build
phases.note: Stop 1 to 3 reps short of failure. Add reps or weight every session you can.

phases.name: Deload
phases.note: Half the sets, same weights. Keep the daily physio work.

phases.name: Build, harder
phases.note: Priority exercises (marked) get a 4th set: chest, shoulders and arms. Isolation work can go to failure.

phases.name: Deload and retest
phases.note: Half sets in the first two sessions. Retest in the last session: max push ups, goblet squat reps, single arm row reps.

gymLater.name: Half kneeling single arm overhead press

steps: Hold one dumbbell upright against your chest, hands cupped under the top end.
Feet hip width, toes turned out. Ribs down, pelvis tucked.
Sit down between your heels over 3 seconds, knees following your toes, chest up.
Go as deep as you can while holding that position, then stand up in about 1 second.
Put one hand and the same knee on a bench, sofa or sturdy chair. Other foot on the floor, back flat.
Let the dumbbell hang under your shoulder. Set the shoulder blade back and tuck your chin.
Pull your elbow towards your back pocket and squeeze for 1 second.
Lower over 3 seconds. Do all your reps, then switch sides.
Lie on your back on the floor, knees bent, a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing each other.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down into the floor.
Press the dumbbells straight up over your chest.
Lower until your upper arms lightly touch the floor, pause, then press again.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, knees soft.
Push your hips back and slide the dumbbells down your thighs. Keep your back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, usually around or just below the knee.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand up. Do not lean back at the top.
Hold a band at shoulder height, arms straight, hands shoulder width apart, thumbs up.
Set your shoulder blades back and tuck your chin.
Pull the band apart until it touches your chest and hold for 2 seconds.
Return slowly. Keep your shoulders down, no shrugging.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and your shoulder blades back.
Curl the dumbbells up without turning your palms.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
Lie on your back with your knees bent at 90 degrees above your hips and your shins level (the table top).
Gently press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly straighten one leg out towards the floor, then bring it back. Alternate legs.
Stop the set when your lower back starts to lift. This is your physio exercise, so if your sheet shows it differently, follow the sheet.
Stand about a stride in front of a chair or sofa and rest the top of your back foot on it.
Hold the dumbbells at your sides. Turn your front foot slightly out if that feels better.
Lower straight down until your back knee is near the floor, front knee tracking over your toes.
Push through your front foot to stand up. Do all your reps, then switch legs.
rfe_split_squat.video: rear foot elevated split squat dumbbell form

steps: Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides, feet hip width, toes slightly out.
Step one foot back and lower until your back knee is near the floor.
Keep your front knee tracking over your toes. Do not let your back leg cross the midline.
Push through your front foot to step back up. Step up option: step onto a sturdy step or bench instead.
Lie face down on a bench, or with your chest over the arm of a sofa or the end of a bed. Let a dumbbell hang from each hand.
Set your shoulder blades back and tuck your chin.
Pull both elbows back towards your back pockets and pause for 1 second.
Lower over 3 seconds.
Put your hands slightly wider than your shoulders, body straight from head to heels, ribs down, glutes squeezed.
Lower your chest to the floor with control, elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Push back up.
Too hard: put your hands on a worktop. Too easy: put your feet on a chair.
Hinge forward from your hips with a flat back, a light dumbbell in each hand hanging under your chest.
Point your thumbs forward and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they're level with your body, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower slowly.
Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the dumbbells up to your shoulders.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight, then go straight into the tricep extension.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands under the top end, arms straight above your head. Sit or stand tall, ribs down.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Straighten back up. If your shoulder feels pinched, swap to the lying version from Session B.
tricep_ext.video: overhead dumbbell tricep extension two hands

steps: Hold one heavy dumbbell at your side, like a suitcase.
Stand tall, ribs down, pelvis level. Do not lean towards the weight.
Walk slowly for the set time, then swap hands.
Side plank option: lie on your side, forearm under your shoulder, lift your hips into a straight line and hold.
Stand facing a wall with your palm on it at shoulder height.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and tuck your chin.
Tuck your pelvis and step your feet back so you lean into the stretch.
Hold 10 seconds. This is your physio exercise, so follow the photo on your sheet.
Hold a band with both hands in front of you.
Set your shoulder blades back and tuck your chin.
Pull the band apart evenly and hold 10 seconds, at chest height, then low, then high.
This is your physio exercise, so follow the photos on your sheet.
Hold a 2.5 kg dumbbell with your elbow bent to 90 degrees.
Set your shoulder blade back and tuck your chin.
Pull your elbow back towards the opposite back pocket and hold 6 seconds.
Do 10 reps each side. Follow your physio sheet for the exact position.
Put a band around your forefeet, feet hip width.
Bend your knees slightly, ribs down, pelvis tucked.
Take 3 steps sideways, keeping tension on the band, then 3 steps back.
Do 2 rounds. Follow your physio sheet.
Pick the first exercise of the session.
Do one easy set at about half your working weight.
Use it to practise the position and cues, not to tire yourself out.
Stand side on to a table. Put one hand on it and step that same leg forward, back leg straight behind you.
Hinge forward with a flat back. Let the dumbbell hang under your shoulder in the other hand.
Set the shoulder blade back, tuck your chin and pull your elbow towards your back pocket. Squeeze for 1 second.
Lower over 3 seconds. Do all your reps, then switch sides.
split_row.video: split stance single arm dumbbell row

steps: Hands on a kitchen worktop or sturdy table, slightly wider than your shoulders. Walk your feet back until your body is straight.
Set your shoulder blades back and down, ribs down, glutes squeezed.
Lower your chest to the edge with control, elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Push back up until your arms are straight. Stop there, no extra push at the top. Lower surface = harder.
Stand with one hand on a table, opposite foot back, flat back, dumbbell in the free hand.
Pin that upper arm to your side, elbow bent to 90 degrees, shoulder blade back.
Straighten your arm behind you, moving only at the elbow. Squeeze for 1 second.
Lower back to 90 degrees under control. Do all your reps, then switch sides.
Hold one dumbbell at your side like a suitcase. Stand tall, ribs down, pelvis level.
Slowly lift one knee to hip height, put it down, then the other.
Don't lean towards the weight or let your hips drop.
March for the set time, then swap hands.
